open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:owner_sign_in_and_session`
open_points.question: Which operation calls `give_owner_credential`, and is it called once during start or by `sign_in_owner` for each sign-in?
options: `capability:owner_sessions.sign_in_owner` calls it for every unlocked sign-in
`capability:instance_lifecycle.start_instance` calls it once and supplies the credential to `module:owner_sessions`
`module:configuration` pushes the credential to `module:owner_sessions` during configuration loading
open_points.default_guess: Have `capability:owner_sessions.sign_in_owner` call it when performing the credential comparison.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:owner_sign_in_and_session`
open_points.question: Can `give_owner_credential` fail after a successful start, and, if so, what outcome does the sign-in flow produce?
options: It is total after configuration has loaded and has no failure
The sign-in is refused with the same answer as a wrong credential
The instance treats failure as an internal invariant failure and stops serving
open_points.default_guess: Make it total after the successful configuration check.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:owner_sign_in_and_session`
open_points.text: `module:configuration` gives the checked owner credential to `module:owner_sessions` alone
open_points.question: Does “alone” exclude the loading and checking modules, or does it literally mean that no module other than `module:owner_sessions` may receive the credential?
options: It excludes only operational consumers; `module:runtime_settings` and `module:configuration` may handle it while loading and checking
Only `module:owner_sessions` may ever receive it, requiring configuration loading and checking without exposing its value to those modules
open_points.default_guess: Treat `module:runtime_settings` and `module:configuration` as permitted loading/checking intermediaries and forbid every other operational consumer.

witness.initial: The host has a valid owner credential in a complete configuration and Registry is stopped.
events: `module:runtime_settings` reads the owner credential from the environment and supplies it in the settings.
`module:configuration` receives and checks it, then supplies it to `module:owner_sessions`.
outcomes: The changed flow can be read to say that `module:owner_sessions` alone receives the credential.
`flow:start_instance` says the credential enters `module:runtime_settings`, leaves in the settings to `module:configuration`, and is then handed to its using module.
witness.observer: A security reviewer or module-boundary test observing which modules handle the credential.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:service_reads_project`
open_points.question: Which operation calls `give_service_tokens`, and is it called once during start or by `identify_service` for each service request?
options: `capability:instance_lifecycle.start_instance` calls it once and supplies the token table to `module:service_access`
`module:configuration` pushes the token table to `module:service_access` during configuration loading
open_points.default_guess: Have `capability:service_access.identify_service` call it when performing token identification.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:service_reads_project`
open_points.question: Can `give_service_tokens` fail after a successful non-owner-only start, and, if so, what outcome does the service request produce?
options: It is total after configuration has loaded and has no failure
The request is refused exactly like an unknown token
The instance treats failure as an internal invariant failure and stops serving
open_points.default_guess: Make it total after the successful configuration check.

open_points.subject: 40_flows.md:`flow:service_reads_project`
open_points.text: `module:configuration` gives it the checked tokens, and no other module receives them
open_points.question: Are `module:runtime_settings` and `module:configuration` exceptions to “no other module receives them,” or must the token-loading path be redesigned so only `module:service_access` receives token values?
options: The phrase means no other operational consumer; the loading and checking modules may receive the tokens
No module other than `module:service_access` may receive token values
`module:configuration` may receive them but `module:runtime_settings` may not
open_points.default_guess: Allow `module:runtime_settings` and `module:configuration` as loading/checking intermediaries, while making `module:service_access` the sole operational recipient.

witness.initial: Registry is stopped and the environment contains all four valid service tokens and the service API address.
events: `module:runtime_settings` reads the service-token environment items and supplies them in the settings.
`module:configuration` receives and checks the tokens, then gives them to `module:service_access`.
outcomes: The changed service flow says no module other than `module:service_access` receives the tokens.
`flow:start_instance` says the environment items enter `module:runtime_settings`, leave as settings to `module:configuration`, and are then handed on as loaded configuration.
witness.observer: A security reviewer or module-boundary test observing which modules receive service-token values.
